subject: Use Multiple Different Dataset in Parallel

messages.author: 89a4640ddc6e46d0
messages.subject: Use Multiple Different Dataset in Parallel
parts:
Hi,

I would like to run the same model, on many simulated datasets. I have created a list of datalists (foo_data).

I will run the program on a red hat linux cluster.

I haven't seen code for this situation, and was hoping someone could correct (or confirm) my code. In particular, I am not sure of how to properly set the seed in this case?

library(parallel)
library(rstan)


foo_data <- ...; #this will be a list of datalists
rng_seed <- ...;
foo <- stan("foo.stan", data = foo_data[[1]], chains = 0)




big_foo<- function(dat){
  modfit<-stan(fit = foo, data = dat, seed = rng_seed, chains = 1, refresh = -1)
  elem<-mean(extract(modfit)$gamma[,1])
  return(elem)
}


sflist <- mclapply(foo_data, mc.cores = 10, big_foo)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Use Multiple Different Dataset in Parallel
parts:
Someone else will have to tell you how to code this best in R,
but the best thing to do is provide a single seed and then give
each parallel execution a different chain ID, (argument chain_id=<int> to stan())
which will advance the (P)RNG far enough that they draw from different parts of
a very large sequence.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: Use Multiple Different Dataset in Parallel
parts:
I needed to do something similar (multiple imputation datasets) and found this thread in the process.  I ended up with:

## data_list is a list of 16 datasets, each replicated 3 times (so each data set gets 3 chains)

compile <- stan(model_code = model_code, data = delay_imp_dat_list[[1]], init = "random", chains = 0)
chains <- 48
cl <- makeCluster(chains, type = "SOCK")
clusterExport(cl, list=c("delay_imp_dat_list", "compile", "chains"))
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(rstan))
model_fit <- parLapply(cl, 1:chains, fun = function(chain) {
    stan(fit = compile, seed=123, data = data_list[[chain]], chains = 1, warmup=500, iter=5500, verbose = TRUE, init = "random", refresh = -1, chain_id=chain)
    })
stopCluster(cl)
model_fit <- sflist2stanfit(model_fit)

Katherine
